notebook.definition: a book of blank or ruled pages used for writing.
examples: Write your notes in the notebook.

niece.definition: the daughter of one’s brother or sister; a female nephew.
examples: Her niece visited last summer.

nephew.definition: the son of your brother or sister.
examples: Her nephew learned to ride a bike.
We invited my nephew to the game.

nurse.definition: a healthcare worker who gives care to patients in hospitals or clinics
examples: The nurse brought a blanket.
He is a nurse at the local hospital.

nurse.definition: to provide care and support for someone over time
examples: She nursed her brother back to health.
He nursed a sore throat for days.
The city lies north of here.
Look to the north.

north.definition: in or toward the north direction
examples: They drove north for two hours.
The train moves north in the morning.
Owls are nocturnal birds.
The animal is nocturnal.

novel.definition: a long work of fiction with characters and a plot
examples: She wrote a new novel.
The novel is set in the 1800s.

novel.definition: new or original in a way that has not been seen before
examples: It was a novel idea for the project.
She left a note on my desk.
I found a note in the book.

note.definition: a single sound with a specific pitch in music
examples: The piano played a high note.
That note is hard to sing.

note.definition: to notice or pay attention to something
examples: Did you note the change in schedule?
I noted her name in my notebook.

noon.definition: the middle of the day when the sun is highest
examples: Meet me at noon.
The store closes at noon.

navigator.definition: a person who plans and directs the route of a ship, aircraft, or spacecraft
examples: The navigator checked the weather before the flight.
A good navigator helps avoid dangerous areas.
The navigator’s log recorded the course changes.

nautical.definition: related to ships, sailors, or navigation by sea
examples: They studied nautical charts for the voyage.
The captain gave a nautical briefing.
He is nimble on the basketball court.
A nimble worker can learn tasks quickly.

nominate.definition: to formally suggest someone for election, appointment, or an award
examples: They nominated him for the position.
The committee nominated three candidates.

narrate.definition: to tell a story or describe events in order
examples: She narrated her experience in detail.
The film narrator helps you follow the plot.
Her handwriting is neat.
Make sure the books are kept neat.
She was nettled by the rude comment.
He looked nettled when they changed the rules.

nonsense.definition: ideas or statements that do not make sense
examples: That’s nonsense; the facts are different.
Stop spreading nonsense.

nag.definition: to keep asking someone repeatedly to do something, especially in an annoying way
examples: She nags her brother to tidy his room.
Don’t nag me about it.

nag.definition: a repeated annoying request or complaint
examples: It was just a nag about homework.

needlelike.definition: shaped like a needle; long, thin, and pointed
examples: The needlelike spikes hurt when touched.
The metal was needlelike and sharp.

numinous.definition: seemingly full of spiritual power or mystery
examples: The numinous atmosphere of the temple made people quiet.
She felt a numinous presence in the old forest.

near.definition: not far away in distance, time, or amount.
examples: The store is near my house.
The deadline is near.

near.definition: in a nearby place or time.
examples: Come and meet me near the entrance.
It’s near impossible to finish today.

nah.definition: a casual way to say no, especially to refuse something
examples: Nah, I’m not coming tonight.
He said nah and hung up.
Her response was just a quick nah.
I gave him a firm nah.

nascent.definition: just beginning and not fully formed or developed
examples: A nascent technology is gaining attention.
The company is in a nascent phase.

navigate.definition: to plan and direct a route through an area, especially while traveling
examples: We navigated the city using GPS.
She navigated the boat safely through the channel.

navigate.definition: to deal with a situation successfully, especially one that is complex
examples: He helped us navigate the difficult contract.
They navigated their way through the negotiations.

notation.definition: a system of symbols or marks used to write information, especially in math or music
examples: The notation for fractions is easy to learn.
She used music notation to write the melody.

natter.definition: to talk in a silly or continuous way, often about unimportant things
examples: Stop nattering and listen for a minute.
They nattered about movies all evening.

neigh.definition: to make the sound that a horse makes
examples: The horse neighed when the rider approached.
I heard a neigh in the stable.

nab.definition: to catch someone or get something quickly, often by surprise
examples: The police nabbed the suspect near the station.
She nabbed a good deal at the sale.

niggardly.definition: unwilling to give or spend money in a way that seems unfairly small
examples: She was called niggardly for refusing extra help.
They offered a niggardly amount of funding.

nonsequitur.definition: a statement or answer that does not logically follow from what was said before
examples: His response was a nonsequitur, so nobody understood the point.
The judge said the argument was a nonsequitur.

nicking.definition: a small cut or notch made in a surface
examples: He got a nick on his finger while cutting the paper.
The paint has a small nick near the handle.

nicking.definition: to make a small cut or notch
examples: I nicked the edge of the table while moving it.
Be careful not to nick the cable.

nay.definition: used to mean no, especially in formal or traditional speech
examples: The mayor said nay to the proposal.
He answered nay when asked to sign.

notion.definition: an idea or belief about something
examples: I have a notion that we should start earlier.
It’s a common notion that exercise helps stress.

nation.definition: a country considered as a political community or as its people
examples: The nation elected a new government.
Many nations have similar holidays.

native.definition: a person who was born in a particular country or place
examples: She is a native of Canada.
He became friends with the native students.

native.definition: belonging naturally to a place or country
examples: This plant is native to the region.
My grandfather grew up in the area and knew the native animals.

nicker.definition: a soft sound made by a horse
examples: The horse gave a nicker as we approached.
I heard a nicker from the stable.

nicker.definition: to make a soft sound like a horse
examples: The mare nickered when she saw the food.
The pony nickered to get attention.

nicked.definition: having a small cut or scratch, or being lightly damaged
examples: He had a nicked finger from the box cutter.
The paper was nicked at the corner.

niggardliness.definition: extreme unwillingness to spend money or share, often in a petty way
examples: Her niggardliness kept her from tipping even a little.
He was known for his niggardliness with coworkers.
The natal chart is used in astrology.
Her natal family moved to another city.

nature.definition: the natural world, including plants, animals, weather, and land
examples: We walked in nature to relax.
Nature is beautiful in spring.

nature.definition: the basic character or qualities of something
examples: The nature of the job is stressful.
She understood the nature of his problem.

nature.definition: the physical forces that control living things
examples: Nature controls how species adapt.
In nature, balance matters.

nap.definition: a short sleep during the day
examples: I took a nap after lunch.
She had a short nap before studying.

nap.definition: to sleep for a short time
examples: He napped for 20 minutes.
Try to nap before the trip.

notary.definition: a public official who verifies signatures and legal documents
examples: The notary verified the signatures.
We went to a notary to finalize the document.

nocturne.definition: a musical piece that suggests night or is often played at night
examples: We listened to a nocturne on the piano.
Her favorite composer wrote many nocturnes.

noctambule.definition: a person who stays awake or moves around at night
examples: He’s a noctambule who works late at night.
The character is a noctambule in the story.
